sections.h2: Does every Iowa house go through probate?
sections.html:
No. An estate does not have to be opened for every person who dies. One may be needed to transfer property, pay debts or obtain tax clearances, and a house titled only in the decedent's name usually needs some court step before it can be sold or retitled.

Probate in Iowa runs through the district court in the county, and the clerk of court is the first office to call. A valid will must be in writing, signed by the maker and witnessed by two people. If you cannot find a will, ask the clerk in the county where it may be stored, any attorney who drafted it, and the named executor, and check safe deposit boxes.

sections.h2: Who can open an Iowa estate, and how soon?
sections.html:
A surviving spouse, an heir, a creditor or another person with good grounds may petition for appointment. Iowa Code 633.227 and 633.228 give priority by class: the surviving spouse has 20 days from the death to file, and each other class has 10 days, with a class's window moving up if nobody exists in the class before it.

Whoever serves must be a natural person of full age, not incompetent and not found unsuitable by the court (633.63). "Full age" means 18, or having married (633.3). A court can remove a fiduciary on a verified petition under 633.65.

With several heirs, agree early on who will be the personal representative. That person signs the sale papers and answers to the court.

The statute sets several clocks that matter to a family planning to sell a house.

Estate stepDeadline or cost
Hearing noticeAt least 20 days after service, unless good cause shortens it
Inventory and report90 days after the personal representative qualifies, unless extended
Creditor claimsLater of four months after the second published notice or one month after mailed notice
Spouse's electionFour months after service of notice
Court cost0.2% of probate assets listed in the inventory
Outside limit for openingClaims are barred if administration has not started within five years of death
Delinquent filingsClerk notices go out June 1 and December 1; 60 days to file

The 0.2% court cost leaves out joint tenancy property, lifetime transfers, life insurance payable to a beneficiary and real estate outside Iowa. The sections are 633.40, 633.361, 633.410, 633.237, 633.31, 633.413 and 633.32, in table order.

sections.h2: Who inherits an Iowa house with no will?
sections.html:
Iowa intestacy law sends the house first to a surviving spouse, then down a list of relatives. The split depends on whether the children are also the spouse's children.

  • No children, or all children shared with the spouse: the spouse takes the real property the decedent held during the marriage, subject to exceptions such as judicial sales (633.211).
  • Some children are not the spouse's: the spouse takes one half of the real property, and the estate tops up the spouse's total to $50,000 if the share falls short (633.212).
  • No spouse: the order runs to children, then parents, then siblings' descendants, then grandparents, then great-grandparents, and finally escheat to the state (633.219).

In an intestate estate the spouse may elect a life estate in the homestead instead (633.240). A homestead inside a city plat is limited to one half acre, and outside a plat to forty acres (561.2).

sections.h2: When the personal representative can sell the house
sections.html:
The personal representative can sell estate real estate to pay debts, distribute the estate or serve the estate's best interests. Exempt personal property and the homestead are carved out and follow their own rules (633.386). If the homestead is not set off to the spouse and the spouse has not chosen to occupy it, it can be sold under the court-directed provisions.

Know these features of a sale before you speak with a buyer:

  • Notice of a sale petition goes to interested persons unless they waive it in writing or all of them are personal representatives who signed the petition (633.389).
  • A sale on credit for more than twelve months needs a hearing on notice (633.392).
  • A public auction is advertised once a week for two consecutive weeks in a county newspaper, with the last notice one to seven days before the sale (633.397).
  • Sale proceeds are held by the personal representative, subject to any rights of the spouse or children, unless those rights are waived (633.386).

A title company or buyer may ask the representative to prove authority. Under 633.78, a third party has 10 business days to verify a fiduciary's authority, and an unjustified refusal can lead to penalties from $500 to $10,000 plus damages.

sections.h2: The small estate affidavit and a house
sections.html:
Iowa's affidavit procedure for very small estates applies only if the decedent's personal property totals $50,000 or less and there is no real property. A house is real property, so this shortcut rarely works for a family that wants to sell one.

The procedure also needs at least forty days to have passed since the death, a sworn affidavit and a certified death certificate, and it cannot be used while an administration is pending (633.356). For deaths before January 1, 2025, real property passing to people exempt from inheritance tax as joint tenants with survivorship rights also qualified.

If the house was held in joint tenancy with a surviving owner, no probate may be needed to move title. Ask the county recorder or an attorney what filing proves the survivor's ownership.

sections.h2: Creditor claims and a house sale
sections.html:
Creditors have a limited window to file, and that window shapes when an estate can safely close. Notice is published once a week for two weeks in a local newspaper, and known claimants whose claims may not be paid in administration receive mailed notice (633.230).

Claims not filed by the later of four months after the second publication or one month after mailing are barred, with statutory exceptions (633.410). The representative may still pay valid debts that were never filed, at the representative's own risk (633.435). Property other than the homestead and exempt property is chargeable with the debts and costs of the estate (633.350).

Heirs who want a fast sale should talk to the estate's attorney before distributing money. A house sold early can pay the debts, and the remainder can be shared.

sections.h2: Does Iowa still have an inheritance tax?
sections.html:
No tax applies to estates of people who died on or after January 1, 2025. Section 450.98 says the chapter does not apply to the property of those decedents.

The old rules still matter for deaths before 2025. Spouses, lineal ascendants and descendants and stepchildren were exempt. Brothers, sisters and in-laws paid graduated rates from 5% to 10%, and other individuals paid 10% to 15%. The tax was due nine months after death and was a lien on the estate for up to ten years. A sale by a personal representative under a will's power or a court order removed the lien from the property and moved it to the proceeds (450.6, 450.7, 450.10).

For an older death, ask whether a receipt or certificate of nonliability was filed with the clerk of court.

sections.h2: Options for selling an inherited Iowa house
sections.html:
An heir with legal authority can list the house on the open market, sell it at auction under court rules, or accept an as-is cash offer. Each route requires the same proof of who may sign.

A cash buyer can often close quickly, which suits families who live out of state or share a house among siblings. Whichever buyer you choose, confirm the following in writing:

  • Letters of appointment, or proof that survivorship title passed.
  • Whether the will gives a power of sale, which changes the court steps.
  • Property tax status and any special assessments.
  • Who will receive proceeds, and in what order creditors are paid.

Cash Home Buyers buys inherited houses as they are, so heirs do not have to clean out, repair or stage the home before closing. Gather the letters of appointment, the death certificate and the latest tax statement first, and the title company can tell you what else it needs.

faqs.q: How long does probate take in Iowa?
faqs.a: Length varies. Main checkpoints include the 90-day inventory deadline after the personal representative qualifies and a creditor claim window of at least four months. Most estates with a house last longer than those checkpoints, depending on sales and disputes.

faqs.q: Can an Iowa heir sell a house before probate ends?
faqs.a: Yes, if the personal representative has authority to sell and follows the court or will provisions. A will that gives a power of sale changes the procedure, and a buyer will want letters of appointment.

faqs.q: Is there a small estate shortcut for a house in Iowa?
faqs.a: Usually no. The affidavit for very small estates requires $50,000 or less in personal property and no real property. A house is real property, so formal administration is likely.

faqs.q: Does Iowa charge inheritance tax now?
faqs.a: Not for deaths on or after January 1, 2025. Estates of people who died earlier may still involve the old tax and lien rules.

faqs.q: What does an Iowa probate cost in court fees?
faqs.a: The court cost under Iowa Code 633.31 is 0.2% of the probate assets listed in the inventory for most estate services. It leaves out joint tenancy property, lifetime transfers and life insurance payable to a named beneficiary. Attorney and fiduciary fees are separate costs of administration.
